answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding for work, and caps its total open contracts in proportion to that bond. An attacker running agents named nebula, zephyr, and falcon gains no extra capacity by splitting one bond among them: the same capital buys the same total contract limit. To scale a sybil swarm, the attacker must lock proportionally more money, tying up funds for as long as the contracts remain open.
